Rashi on Sotah 23b:10:1.hebrew: ורגמו אותו - אי נימא "אותו" ולא אותה, והכתיב גבי נערה המאורסה: "והוצאתם את שניהם ... וסקלתם אותם"? אלא הא דממעט אשה לענין ערום, דנפיק מהאי קרא — מיעוטא דאותו משמע ולא כסותו. ולהכי נקט ליה להאי משמעותא דערום בלשון זכר גבי איש, למימרא הא אותה בכסותה:
Rashi on Sotah 23b:10:1.english: And they shall stone him - If we were to say [that "him" excludes women, i.e.] "him" and not her — but isn't it written regarding a betrothed girl: "And you shall bring them both out ... and you shall stone them"? Rather, [the point is that] the exclusion of a woman with regard to [being stoned] naked, which is derived from this verse, [is as follows]: the limiting term "him" implies "him" and not his clothing. And therefore it expressed this implication of nakedness in the masculine form regarding a man — to say that [as for] her, [she is stoned] in her clothing:

Rashi on Sotah 23b:12:1.hebrew: נמכר בגניבתו - אם אין לו מה לשלם:
Rashi on Sotah 23b:12:1.english: Is sold for his theft - If he has nothing with which to pay.

Rashi on Sotah 23b:14:1.english: A betrothed woman - Whose betrothed husband warned her [against seclusion with another man].

Rashi on Sotah 23b:14:2.english: And a woman awaiting her yavam - [This refers to one] whose yavam warned her [not to be secluded with a particular man].

Rashi on Sotah 23b:14:3.english: They do not drink - For the verse excluded them.

Rashi on Sotah 23b:14:4.hebrew: ולא נוטלות כתובה - שהיא גרמה לאסור עצמה עליו, שנסתרה אחר קינוי. דמקינוי ואיסור לא אימעיט, כדמפרש בגמרא. ואפילו לית לן דרב המנונא דשומרת יבם שזינתה מותרת ליבמה — נהי דמותרת, מיהו לא בעי למינסב אשה זונה, והיא הפסידה כתובתה:
Rashi on Sotah 23b:14:4.english: And they do not collect a ketubah - For she caused herself to be forbidden to him, since she secluded herself after being warned [by her husband]. For [the prohibition] is not excluded from [the law of] warning and prohibition, as the Gemara explains. And even if we do not hold [in accordance with] Rav Hamnuna's [ruling] that a widow awaiting her yavam who committed adultery is permitted to her yavam — granted that she is permitted, nevertheless he does not want to marry a promiscuous woman, and she herself forfeited her ketubah:

Rashi on Sotah 23b:14:5.hebrew: תחת אישה - ביושבת תחתיו הכתוב מדבר:
Rashi on Sotah 23b:14:5.english: Under her husband - The verse is speaking of one who dwells under him [i.e., is married to him].

Rashi on Sotah 23b:1:1.hebrew: ה"ג ואפי' רבנן לא פליגי עליה אלא במנחת חוטא של כהנים דבת הקרבה היא - דמקשי חובתו לנדבתו דלא בעי קמיצה. אבל הא דלאו בת הקרבה היא, דדלמא בתרה דידה אזלינן, ושירים גמורים נינהו, ואפילו רבנן מודו דמתפזרין:
Rashi on Sotah 23b:1:1.english: This is the text: "And even the Rabbis disagree with him only regarding the sin-offering meal-offering of priests, since it is [a case] of offering - For they compare its obligatory [offering] to its voluntary [offering], which does not require the removal of a handful (kemitzah). But this [case, the meal-offering of a priest's wife], which is not [a case] of offering, [the reason is] that perhaps we follow after her, and they are complete remainders (shirayim), and even the Rabbis concede that they are scattered."

Rashi on Sotah 23b:2:1.hebrew: מאי טעמא - קאמר מתני': מנחת כהנת נאכלת כשאינה נשואה לכהן, וכשהיא נשואה לכהן אינה נאכלת. כליל מיהא לא הויא:
Rashi on Sotah 23b:2:1.english: What is the reason? - The Mishnah says: The meal-offering of a priest's daughter is eaten when she is not married to a priest, and when she is married to a priest it is not eaten. [But] at any rate, it is not [offered as] a whole burnt offering.

Rashi on Sotah 23b:3:1.hebrew: לא יחלל זרעו - בכהן הנושא פסולה לכהונה כתיב, ודרשינן בקידושין (דף עז.): לא יחלל — שני חילולין, אחד לה ואחד לזרעו. שהכהן מחלל את שתיהן, אבל הוא אין מתחלל:
Rashi on Sotah 23b:3:1.english: He shall not profane his offspring - This is written regarding a priest who marries a woman disqualified from the priesthood, and we expound it in Kiddushin (77a): "He shall not profane" — [this teaches] two profanations, one of her and one of his offspring. For a priest profanes both of them, but he himself is not profaned.

Rashi on Sotah 23b:4:1.hebrew: בני אהרן - "לנפש לא יטמא", ולא בנות אהרן באזהרה זו:
Rashi on Sotah 23b:4:1.english: The sons of Aaron - "He shall not defile himself for a [dead] soul" — but not the daughters of Aaron; they are not included in this warning.

Rashi on Sotah 23b:5:1.hebrew: כל זכר בבני אהרן יאכלנה - במנחה כתיב:
Rashi on Sotah 23b:5:1.english: Every male among the sons of Aaron may eat it - It is written regarding the meal-offering.

Rashi on Sotah 23b:6:1.english: A man - He is a leper.

Rashi on Sotah 23b:6:2.hebrew: אין לי - שנחלט בטומאת נתקים אלא איש. אשה מנין? כשהוא אומר סמוך לו "והצרוע אשר בו הנגע" — ולא איבעי ליה למכתב אלא "בגדיו יהיו פרומים וראשו יהיה פרוע", דהא כתיב לעיל דבמצורע קמיירי — אלא לרבות צרוע שני, כגון אשה:
Rashi on Sotah 23b:6:2.english: I only have - [that one is] declared definitively impure through the impurity of scalls only [in the case of] a man. From where [do we know this for] a woman? When it says right next to it, "And the leper in whom is the affliction" — and [the verse] should have written only, "his garments shall be rent and his head shall be unkempt," since it was already written above that it is speaking of a leper — rather, [the extra phrase comes] to include a second leper, such as a woman.

Rashi on Sotah 23b:7:1.hebrew: ה"ג א"כ מה ת"ל איש לענין שלמטה איש פורע ופורם וכו' - מה תלמוד לומר איש, מאחר שסופינו לרבות את האשה:
Rashi on Sotah 23b:7:1.english: This is the text: If so, why does it say "man"? [It is] for the matter below: "A man lets his hair grow loose and tears [his garments]," etc. - Why does it say "man," given that in the end we include the woman?

Rashi on Sotah 23b:7:2.hebrew: לענין שלמטה - לאו למעוטי מטומאה האמורה בפסוק זה בא למעוטי, אלא מענין האמור בפסוק שלאחריו דכתיב ביה פריעה ופרימה, לומר לך: איש פורע ופורם ולא אשה:
Rashi on Sotah 23b:7:2.english: For the matter below - It does not come to exclude [a woman] from the impurity stated in this verse; rather, [it comes to exclude her] from the matter stated in the verse that follows it, in which loosening [the hair] and tearing [the garments] are written. This is to tell you: a man loosens [his hair] and tears [his garments], but not a woman.

Rashi on Sotah 23b:8:1.english: It is a halakha concerning a nazirite - It is a halakha transmitted to Moses at Sinai, [found] in the laws of the nazirite.

Rashi on Sotah 23b:9:1.english: I gave to a man - The giving of her [in marriage] is dependent on her father.

Tosafot on Sotah 23b:11:1.hebrew: ותלית אותו ולא אותה - בפרק נגמר הדין (סנהדרין דף מו.): נפקא לן מ"וכי יהיה באיש", ולא באשה:
Tosafot on Sotah 23b:11:1.english: "And you shall hang him" – but not her - In the chapter "Nigmar HaDin" (Sanhedrin 46a): We derive it from "And if there be in a man..." – [that it applies] to a man and not to a woman.

Tosafot on Sotah 23b:12:1.hebrew: בגניבתו ולא בגניבתה - תימה: כיון דאי גנבה אינה נמכרת בגניבתה, א"כ אין ב"ד רשאין למוכרה, דבית דין אין מוכרין אלא בגניבתו. ובפ"ק דקידושין (דף יד:) ממעטי רבנן "מורצע את אזנו" — אזנו שלו, ולא אזן של מוכר עצמו; דדוקא מכרוהו בית דין נרצע. ואשה, הואיל ואין בית דין מוכרין אותה, אנא ידענא דאינה נרצעת! ואמאי איצטריך לרבנן למילף מהעבד, ולא אמה העבריה דאינה נרצעת? וי"ל: כיון דאינה נמכרת אלא ע"י אביה, סד"א תיהוי מכירה דאב במקום מכירת בית דין, ותרצע — להכי איצטריך קרא:
Tosafot on Sotah 23b:12:1.english: For his theft, but not for her theft - This is puzzling: Since, if she stole, she is not sold for her theft, it follows that the court is not permitted to sell her, for the court sells only for [a man's] theft. And in the first chapter of Kiddushin (14b), the Rabbis exclude [from the verse] "his ear shall be pierced": "his ear" means his own ear, and not the ear of one who sold himself; for only one whom the court sold has his ear pierced. Now a woman — since the court does not sell her — I already know that she does not have her ear pierced! So why did the Rabbis need to derive [this] from the [Hebrew] slave, and [why do they] not [derive it from] the Hebrew maidservant, who does not have her ear pierced? And one can answer: Since she is sold only by her father, one might have thought that the father's sale should take the place of a court sale, and she should have her ear pierced; therefore the verse was needed.

Tosafot on Sotah 23b:14:1.hebrew: ושומרת יבם לא שותות ולא נוטלות כתובה - ירושלמי: יודעת היתה שאין ארוסה שותה, ולמה הכניסה עצמה למספר הזה המרובה? בשביל לפוסלה מכתובתה. פר"ח: ארוסה, אע"פ שאין לה כתובה, יש לה מנה ומאתים, ועל מנה ומאתים קתני הכא "לא נוטלת כתובתה". רש"י פי': דליכא למיפשט ממתני' הא דאמר רב המנונא שומרת יבם שזנתה אסורה ליבמה, דאפילו אי לית לן דרב המנונא, מיהו אי לא בעי יבם למינסב אשה זונה — אינה נוטלת כתובתה. מיהו תימה: אי לית לן דרב המנונא, קרא מאי איצטריך למעוטי? והא תנן בפרק היה מביא (לעיל סוטה דף יח:): "כל שתיבעל ולא תהא אסורה לו" — לא היה מתנה! דמה קינוי שייך היכא דלא מיתסרא בסתירותיה? אלא מדאיצטריך למעוטי, ש"מ דמיתסרא. מיהו ליכא למיפשט מהכא, משום דמוקי לה בגמרא כגון שבא עליה יבם בבית אחיו, דקנאה לפוטרה בגט בלא חליצה אפילו אליבא דשמואל; הלכך שייכא נמי אשתו ליאסר עליו בזנות כדברי הכל:
Tosafot on Sotah 23b:14:1.english: "And a shomeret yavam neither drinks nor receives her ketubah" - The Yerushalmi [asks]: She knew that a betrothed woman does not drink; why, then, did she bring herself into this large group? [Answer:] In order to disqualify her from her ketubah. Rabbeinu Chaim [explains]: A betrothed woman, even though she has no ketubah, has a maneh and two hundred [zuz], and it is regarding the maneh and two hundred that [the Mishnah] teaches here that she "does not receive her ketubah." Rashi explains that one cannot infer from the Mishnah what Rav Hamnuna said, that a shomeret yavam who committed adultery is forbidden to her yavam; for even if we did not have [the statement] of Rav Hamnuna, still, if the yavam does not want to take an adulterous woman [as a wife], she does not receive her ketubah. However, it is puzzling: if we did not have [the statement] of Rav Hamnuna, what did the verse need to exclude? Surely we learned in the chapter Haya Meivi (above, Sotah 18b): "Any [woman] who, if she is violated, is not forbidden to him" — [the Mishnah] would not have taught [this]! For what warning is relevant where she is not forbidden through her seclusion? Rather, since [the verse] needed to exclude [her], conclude that she is forbidden. However, one cannot infer this from here, because the Gemara establishes it as a case where the yavam had relations with her in his brother's house, so that he acquired her [as a wife] to the point of exempting her with a get without chalitzah, even according to Shmuel; therefore it is also relevant for his wife to become forbidden to him through adultery, according to everyone.

Tosafot on Sotah 23b:15:1.hebrew: אלמנה לכ"ג וכו' - האי דלא עריב ותני להו: "אלו לא שותות ולא נוטלות כתובתן", ולתני: "ארוסה ושומרת יבם, אלמנה לכ"ג וכו', מעוברת חבירו ומניקת חבירו, ואיילונית, זקינה וכו'" — י"ל: משום הכי פלגינהו, משום דחלוקין בטעמם. מיהו תימה: אמאי לא תנא "מעוברת" בתר בבא דאלמנה לכ"ג, דדמי בטעמא? וה"ל למיתני בתחלת הפרק "אלו לא שותות", ובתר ליחשב וליזל כולהו כל הני דדמיין להדדי. כל חד וטפי הוה שייך למיתני "אלו" בראש כולן, ממאי דתני קצת דלא שותות, והדר תני "אלו":
Tosafot on Sotah 23b:15:1.english: A widow [married] to a High Priest, etc. - Why did [the Mishnah] not combine them and teach: "These neither drink nor collect their ketubah," and then teach: "A betrothed woman and a woman awaiting her yavam, a widow [married] to a High Priest, etc., a woman pregnant by her fellow's [husband] and a woman nursing her fellow's [child], and an *ayilonit*, an elderly woman, etc."? One can answer: The reason it separated them is that they differ in their reasons. Nevertheless, it is puzzling: Why did it not teach "a pregnant woman" after the clause of "a widow [married] to a High Priest," since it is similar in reasoning? And it should have taught at the beginning of the chapter "These do not drink," and afterward list and proceed through all of those that resemble one another. It would all the more have been fitting to teach "these" at the head of all of them, rather than teaching some who do not drink and only then teaching "these."

Tosafot on Sotah 23b:2:1.hebrew: כהן ולא כהנת - ירושלמי: ר' אבהו בעי קמיה ר"ל: והכתיב (ויקרא כ״ב:י״א) "וכהן כי יקנה נפש קנין כספו", מעתה כהן ולא כהנת? א"ל: "והכהן המשיח תחתיו מבניו" — את שבנו עומד תחתיו; יצתה זו שאין בנה עומד תחתיה. ה"ה דבפרק הזרוע (חולין דף קלב.) הוה מצי לשנויי נמי הכי: "ונתן לכהן הזרוע" — דלא אמר "לכהן ולא לכהנת", אלא אפילו לכהנת. דהכא טעמא משום דכתיב "והכהן המשיח תחתיו מבניו"; אבל התם דחי ליה משום דאהרן ובניו כתיב בפרשת מנחה, אי נמי משום דהתם הוי מיעוט אחר מיעוט:
Tosafot on Sotah 23b:2:1.english: A priest, and not a priestess - [It is stated] in the Yerushalmi: Rabbi Abahu asked before Resh Lakish: But it is written (Leviticus 22:11), "And if a priest buys a soul, the purchase of his money" — then by that logic, [the verse speaks of] a priest and not a priestess? He said to him: [It is written,] "And the priest who is anointed in his stead from among his sons" — [this refers to one] whose son stands in his stead; this one [a priestess], whose son does not stand in her stead, is excluded. The same is true in the chapter HaZeroa (Chullin 132a): [the Gemara] could have answered there as well in this way: "And he shall give to the priest the shoulder" — for it does not say "to the priest and not to a priestess," but even to a priestess. For here the reason is because it is written, "And the priest who is anointed in his stead from among his sons"; but there it rejected [this answer] because "Aaron and his sons" is written in the passage about the meal-offering, or alternatively because there it would be a limitation following a limitation.

Tosafot on Sotah 23b:6:1.hebrew: מה בין איש לאשה - בתוספתא (פ"ב) קא חשיב: עובר על מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא, מה שאין כן באשה; האיש עובר על בל תקיף ועל בל תשחית ועל בל תטמא למתים, מה שאין כן באשה; האיש נדון בבן סורר ומורה, ונעטף ומספר, ואין האשה נעטפת ומספרת; האיש נמכר ונשנה, ואין האשה נמכרת ונשנית; האיש נרצע ונמכר לעבד עברי וקונה לעבד עברי, ואין האשה נרצעת ונמכרת וקונה. ולא קתני התם כל הני דמתני', אלא דזכאי בבתו, משום דמפרש התם: בכסף ובשטר ובביאה. ותימה: אמאי לא חשיב נמי סמיכות, תנופות, הגשות וקמיצות דבין כהן לכהנת, וכל הני דתנן בפ"ק דקידושין (דף לו.)? ולא קתני נמי שהעברי יוצא בשנים וביובל ובמיתת האדון, משא"כ בעבריה; הזב מטמא בראיות ולא הזבה; מצורע אסור בתשמיש המטה ולא מצורעת, כדמפרש בריש פרק מחוסרי כפרה (כריתות דף ח:); "מחוץ לאהלו" ולא "מחוץ לאהלה":
Tosafot on Sotah 23b:6:1.english: What is the difference between a man and a woman - In the Tosefta (chapter 2) it enumerates: a man transgresses a positive commandment that is time-bound, which is not so for a woman; a man transgresses "you shall not round off [the corners of your head]" and "you shall not destroy [the edge of your beard]" and "he shall not become impure to the dead," which is not so for a woman; a man is judged as a stubborn and rebellious son, and [a man] wraps himself [in a shroud] and cuts his hair [as part of mourning or the nazirite/leper rituals], but a woman does not wrap herself or cut her hair; a man is sold [for his theft] and sold again, but a woman is not sold and sold again; a man has his ear pierced, is sold as a Hebrew slave, and acquires a Hebrew slave, but a woman does not have her ear pierced, is not sold, and does not acquire [a Hebrew slave]. But the Tosefta does not teach there all these [differences] of our Mishnah, except that he is entitled to [act regarding] his daughter, because it explains there: through money, through a document, and through intercourse. And it is astonishing: why does it not also enumerate the laying of hands [on an offering], the waving, the bringing near [to the altar], and the taking of a handful, which distinguish between a priest and a priestess, and all those that we learned in the first chapter of Kiddushin (36a)? And it also does not teach that a Hebrew [male slave] goes free after six years, at the Jubilee, and at the death of the master, which is not so for a Hebrew maidservant; that a male *zav* becomes impure through [counting] sightings, but not a female *zavah*; that a leper is forbidden to marital relations, but not a female leper, as is explained at the beginning of the chapter Mechusrei Kapparah (Keritot 8b); [and that the verse says] "outside his tent" and not "outside her tent."

Tosafot on Sotah 23b:8:1.hebrew: האיש מגלח על נזירות - בפ"ד דנזיר (דף ל.) ובפרק בתרא דכריתות (דף כז:) מפ' דדוקא על מעות סתומין, ולא על מעות מפורשין:
Tosafot on Sotah 23b:8:1.english: A man shaves for [the termination of] nazirite status - In the fourth chapter of Nazir (30a) and in the last chapter of Keritot (27b) it is explained that [this applies] specifically to unspecified coins, and not to specified coins.

Tosafot on Sotah 23b:9:1.hebrew: שנאמר את בתי - מרישא דקרא יליף ליה, ואמר: "אבי הנערה אל הזקנים", משמע למעט אמה, דאינה זכאה בבתה לתת:
Tosafot on Sotah 23b:9:1.english: As it is stated: "My daughter" - [The Gemara] derives it from the beginning of the verse, which says: "The father of the young woman [said] to the elders." This implies that it excludes her mother, who has no right to give her daughter [in betrothal].
